title: Privilege escalation by role assignment
summary: An attacker who took over an account with role-management rights grants itself higher privileges and plants a back-door application.

steps.title: Starting assumption
steps.text: The attacker has taken over a help-desk account that can manage group membership and role assignments.

steps.title: Sign-in evaluated by Conditional Access
steps.text: The account signs in from an unfamiliar address at medium risk. Strong sign-in controls are the last chance to stop it before privileges are changed.

gaps.text: MFA is not enforced for this account, so a stolen password reaches role management.

fix.caTemplate: Require multifactor authentication for all users

steps.whenFixed: Blocked: MFA is required, so the stolen password cannot reach role management.

steps.title: Privileged role granted
steps.text: The attacker adds its account to a privileged role, gaining tenant-wide control. The change takes effect immediately.
steps.whenFixed: The role change is written to the audit log and surfaces for review.

steps.title: Back-door application added
steps.text: The attacker registers a hidden application with broad permissions so access survives password and role cleanup. The application acts on its own, without a user present.
steps.whenFixed: Consent and application-credential controls stop the back-door app from being usable.

outcome.prevented: MFA stops the takeover before any role can be changed.
outcome.notPrevented: The attacker gains tenant-wide control and hides a back-door application.
